chapter: Cliff Jackson, Jelly Roll Morton and Harlem in the 1920s
title: King Oliver and Louis Armstrong's second-trumpet breaks
summary: Caldwell watched Oliver's band and how Armstrong improvised a perfect second part in the two-trumpet breaks.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Oh, yeah, definitely. But I've met Tommy Ladner. Tommy's fine trumpet player. And they had Joe Oliver. Joe Oliver had a thing, they used to do after Louie -- joined him Joe, I mean, lot of guys downtown (unintelligible), come up-town, you know, in Chicago, listen to Joe's band. And they had a thing. We used to get up on the bandstand and watch them. When Joe was going to make a break, like they'd be playing a number like 'Roll Along' different ones, and he'd make the break while the band is playing. But Louie'd catch second on it. So when he'd get to the break for the two trumpets to make it, he had a perfect second to it.
See, but a lot of people didn't know what they were doing.
